intent: What should Carolina Shores homeowners check before installing artificial turf?
distinctValue: Identify the specific community and authority over the proposed area, then distinguish association guidance from Town review.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: the eight communities
supports: The official Town directory names eight communities, including Carolina Shores Subdivision as one of them.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: Carolina Shores Subdivision
supports: The two official community pages describe differing home types; The Acreage is within Carolina Shores Subdivision.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: Calabash Lakes
supports: The two official community pages describe differing home types; The Acreage is within Carolina Shores Subdivision.

supports: Town Planning & Zoning covers zoning, subdivision and floodplain functions in town and ETJ.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: The Village at Calabash
supports: The Village at Calabash is a residential community located on Thomasboro Road.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: frequently asked questions
supports: The fence FAQ tells residents to check HOA/POA permission and then contact the Town about permitting.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: Beacon Townes
supports: Beacon Townes is a townhouse community located on Highway 17.

The Town lists building inspections, planning and zoning, roadway maintenance and solid-waste service for Beacon Townes, with Brunswick County providing water, sewer and law enforcement; no HOA, architectural-review or landscape rule is published on the page.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: Eagle Run
supports: The Town lists the same building inspections, planning and zoning, roadway maintenance and solid-waste service for Eagle Run, with Brunswick County providing water, sewer and law enforcement; no HOA, architectural-review or landscape rule is published on the page.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: Lighthouse Cove
supports: Lighthouse Cove is a residential community located off Thomasboro Road on Carolina Shores' eastern side.

The Town handles building inspections, planning and zoning, roadway maintenance and solid-waste service; Brunswick County provides water, sewer and law enforcement; the page publishes no HOA, architectural-review or landscape rule.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: River Rock at Shingletree
supports: The Town lists building inspections, planning and zoning, street lighting, a solid-waste convenience site and animal control for River Rock at Shingletree — not roadway maintenance, which the Town does list for the other four; the page publishes no HOA, architectural-review or landscape rule.

sources.label: Town of Carolina Shores: The Farm at Brunswick
supports: The Farm at Brunswick is a residential community consisting of single family homes and townhouses.

The Town lists building inspections, planning and zoning, roadway maintenance and solid-waste service, with Brunswick County providing water, sewer and law enforcement; the page publishes no HOA, architectural-review or landscape rule.

claimEvidence.claim: The official Town directory names eight communities, including Carolina Shores Subdivision as one of them.
claimEvidence.source_locator: Communities introductory paragraph and named community links.
claimEvidence.limits: Names establish identity only, not covenant text, HOA membership for a parcel, approval requirements, or coverage of an exact service polygon.
claimEvidence.mappedClaim: Carolina Shores contains several communities, with Carolina Shores Subdivision one of them.

claimEvidence.claim: Town Planning & Zoning covers zoning, subdivision and floodplain functions in town and ETJ.
claimEvidence.source_locator: Planning division introduction and program descriptions.
claimEvidence.limits: No turf-specific code interpretation, universal Town permit requirement or exact parcel jurisdiction is claimed.
claimEvidence.mappedClaim: Ask Town Planning & Zoning about the complete proposal and any grading or drainage changes.

claimEvidence.claim: Calabash Lakes and The Village at Calabash, two of the Town's eight communities, are located on Thomasboro Road.
claimEvidence.source_locator: Community overview paragraph on each page ("...is a residential community located on Thomasboro Road").
claimEvidence.limits: Confirms which two Town communities front Thomasboro Road, not a specific parcel's boundary, mailing address, or which authority (Town vs. county) reviews a given lot. No claim is made about any address outside these two communities.
claimEvidence.mappedClaim: Thomasboro Road runs through two of the Town's eight communities, Calabash Lakes and The Village at Calabash.

claimEvidence.claim: Beacon Townes, Eagle Run, Lighthouse Cove and The Farm at Brunswick are subdivisions inside the Town of Carolina Shores whose Town pages list the same services (building inspections, planning and zoning, roadway maintenance, solid-waste collection, with Brunswick County water/sewer/law enforcement); River Rock at Shingletree's Town page lists building inspections, planning and zoning, street lighting, a solid-waste convenience site and animal control instead. No separate HOA, architectural-review or landscape rule is published on the Town's page for any of the five.
claimEvidence.source_locator: Each community's own Town of Carolina Shores page, town/county services list.
claimEvidence.limits: Absence of published rules on the Town's site does not confirm that no HOA exists for any of these five communities, only that the Town's page does not carry one. The reader is told to ask their own association.
claimEvidence.mappedClaim: Five more of the eight communities — Beacon Townes, Eagle Run, Lighthouse Cove, River Rock at Shingletree and The Farm at Brunswick — are also subdivisions inside the Town; four list the same roadway-maintenance-inclusive town services while River Rock at Shingletree's page lists street lighting, a solid-waste convenience site and animal control instead, with no separate architectural-review or landscape rule published for any of the five.

reviewNotes: Obtain current property/community documents and authorization for the particular area.
